title: The Atom and the Molecule
limitations: The theory of the cubical atom was incomplete in many respects when first designed (p. 767).
The theory lacks a unique or invariable determination of the atomic kernel for certain elements, particularly those not discussed in the paper (p. 769).
The theory does not offer a simple representation for triple bonds with the cubical structure (p. 780).
minimum_safe_summary: This document comprises several chemistry papers from 1916. The initial section, a continuation by Gilbert N. Lewis, details calculations of free-energy values and activity coefficients for hydrochloric acid and potassium chloride, comparing them to conductance ratios and osmotic pressure data. It concludes that activity coefficients decrease more rapidly than conductance ratios at lower concentrations. The subsequent paper, 'The Atom and the Molecule' by Gilbert N. Lewis, proposes a theoretical model of atomic structure, the 'cubical atom,' to explain chemical valence and the distinction between polar and nonpolar substances. It outlines postulates regarding atomic kernels and electron arrangements, particularly the stability of eight electrons. A third empirical study, 'A Study of the Action of Alkali on Certain Zinc Salts by Means of the Hydrogen Electrode' by Joel H. Hildebrand and W. G. Bowers, investigates the reaction of zinc hydroxide with strong alkali to form zincate ions. The entire content is dedicated to chemical principles and experimental findings, with no relevance to the built environment, human cognition, emotion, behavior, or health.
